title: Evaluating LLM Outputs — Grade the Job, Not the Eloquence
key_insight: Write criteria for the actual job: correctness, evidence, completeness, format, and safety where relevant.
body:
## Grade the Job, Not the Eloquence

A polished answer gives the wrong refund policy. Fluency distracted the reviewer from factual failure.

Write criteria for the actual job: correctness, evidence, completeness, format, and safety where relevant.

Collect representative prompts and expected checks before changing prompts or models, so improvements have a stable judge.
common_mistakes: One fluent sample proves production quality.
All good summaries must exactly match one sentence.
A model grader is a permanent ground truth.
mini_exercise: Draw “Grade the Job, Not the Eloquence” as three steps and explain each one.
real_world_usage: Repeatable output evaluation catches quality regressions and separates plausible language from task success.
explain_back_prompt: Use “Grade the Job, Not the Eloquence” to explain Evaluating LLM Outputs plainly.
